title: Monotonicity of the run bound
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$, run on a binary input $x$. If for every output word $o$ some run of at most $b$ steps from label $\ell$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$ reaches $\ell'$, $\rho'$, and $p'$ while appending $e$, and $b\le b'$, then the same endpoints and output extension are reachable within $b'$ steps for every $o$.
hypotheses_covered: A counter program $P$ with $R$ natural-number registers and label set $\Lambda$
A run relation from $\ell,\rho,p$ to $\ell',\rho',p'$ appending $e$ within bound $b$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$ and let $b \le b'$.  If from
label $\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ input symbols read, $P$ reaches
$\ell'$ (a label or the halted state) with registers $\rho'$ and $p'$ symbols
read within $b$ steps while appending $e$ to its output, then it does so within
$b'$ steps as well.
